steps.say: When a calculation has more than one operation, multiply and divide before you add and subtract. 6 + 4 × 3 = 6 + 12 = 18, not 30.
If there are only additions and subtractions, work from left to right. 20 − 5 + 3 = 15 + 3 = 18.
To test for divisibility by 4, look at the last two digits. If they make a number that 4 divides into, the whole number is divisible by 4. 316 works because 16 ÷ 4 = 4.
To test for divisibility by 8, look at the last three digits. 1,128 works because 128 ÷ 8 = 16.
In a sequence that starts at a and adds the same step d each time, the nth term is a + (n − 1) × d.

options.why: Even numbers are not always divisible by 4.
The digit sum is not the test for 4.

hints: Look at the last two digits.
